subject: Discovery follow-up: model fit recommendations + benchmark links
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery follow-up: model fit recommendations + benchmark links

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for a great call earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned on qualification and a small pilot: 

Summary of what we heard from Orion Analytics
- Primary workload: document ingestion + structured extraction for regulatory summaries (avg doc length ~1.8k tokens; 95% are <6k).
- Hard constraints: PII must not leave VPC for pilot; expected concurrency ~8 req/s at peak.
- Quality bar: entity extraction F1 target >= 0.92 on your labeled set; p95 latency target <= 300ms for user-facing summary requests.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist) — based on your throughput/latency targets and cost sensitivity:
1) redwood/gptx-6b-q4f16
   - Why: best mix of generation quality and KV cache-friendly behavior for long-context summarization.
   - Verified profiles: baseline throughput ~420 TPS (tokens/sec) with continuous batching; p50: 80ms, p95: 230ms for 512-token responses on an a100-equivalent node.
2) redwood/opt-2.7b-q8
   - Why: cost-optimized option for high-concurrency extraction-only endpoints (few-shot prompts).
   - Verified profiles: baseline throughput ~950 TPS; p50: 60ms, p95: 190ms for 128-token responses.
3) redwood/llama-medium-q8-4bit (experimental)
   - Why: aggressive quant profile for low-cost batch jobs (async post-processing).
   - Verified profiles: throughput and latency vary by seq-length; suggest using for non-interactive pipelines.

Benchmark and artifacts I attached / linked
- Attachment: redwood-verified-profiles-2028-04.pdf — compact per-model TPS and latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) under test harness mirroring your seq distribution.
- Drive perf CSV: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/ORION-3479/perf-pack-20280402.csv (raw runs, model config, batch sizes).
- Prompt set sample: orion-map-mutation-promptset-1.json (attached) — contains the short/long prompt variants we discussed for extraction and summarization.

Open quality/regression concern that we flagged
- Summaries occasionally hallucinate rare legal clause names when examples are limited. To mitigate: we recommend a small 200-example eval set (we can reuse your labeled subset) and an initial canary rollout to the opt-2.7b profile before moving to gptx-6b for user-facing reads.

Proposed next steps (target timeline)
1) You: share the 200-example labeled eval set (secure upload to the VPC share) by Apr 6.
2) Redwood: we’ll run the two recommended profiles against your eval set and share a per-model regression report by Apr 9.
3) Pilot: 2-week pilot with dedicated capacity (predictable p95 SLO) — pricing estimate and MA will follow once pilot scope is signed.

Please confirm if that timeline works and whether we should loop in legal/infosec for a short call to confirm VPC/KMS details.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-verified-profiles-2028-04.pdf]
[Attachment: orion-map-mutation-promptset-1.json]

From: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@orion-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: model fit recommendations + benchmark links

Thanks Sean — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Quick answers:
- We can share the 200 labeled examples by EOD Apr 5 (secure upload).
- The p95 target of 300ms is firm for interactive summaries; extraction endpoints can be up to 450ms.
- We want the pilot to be in our AWS account (VPC) with customer-managed KMS.

One ask: can you include a short matrix showing expected cost delta between the two recommended profiles (gptx-6b-q4f16 vs opt-2.7b-q8) at our expected volume (avg 4M tokens/month)? That will help procurement.

Thanks,
Aisha
Head of Product
Orion Analytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: model fit recommendations + benchmark links

Hi Aisha —

Looping in a quick cost/ops snapshot. Attached is a 2-slide cost delta (high-level): we estimate ~35% lower token cost on opt-2.7b-q8 for extraction-heavy traffic given your prompt lengths; gptx-6b-q4f16 will be ~1.8x higher in tokens but typically gives better end-user quality for the free-form summarization use cases.

Notes on VPC pilot:
- We support customer-managed KMS and can run the Dedicated pilot in your AWS account.
- Required artifacts for infra: (1) IAM role for Redwood launch, (2) S3 bucket with the eval set (or direct SFTP), (3) expected concurrency and traffic windows.

I'll run the evals once you upload the sample. Expect a per-model PDF with p50/p90/p95/p99, regression deltas against your labeled set, and a short recommendation box.

-Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood

[Attachment: pilot-cost-delta-2sides.pdf]

Appreciate the quick turn. We’ll upload the eval set to the S3 share tonight and I’ve CC’d our infra lead (product@orion-analytics.com) to coordinate IAM.

Two small asks before the run: please include the exact test harness command/flags you use for TPS/latency so our platform team can reproduce locally, and include a short note on how continuous batching settings affect p95 (sounds like it helps heavily at higher concurrency).

If you can include those in the deliverable that would be perfect — then we can move to procurement with a clearer TCO.

Aisha
